title: Rothschild Family: The Documented History
summary: From Frankfurt's Judengasse: Mayer Amschel Rothschild (1744–1812) founded 'M A Rothschild und Söhne' in 1810; five sons built a Europe-wide network underwriting sovereign debt and financing governments including Britain's Napoleonic war effort. Today Rothschild & Co is an advisory/wealth-management firm. It owns no central banks.
tldr: The Rothschild Archive's biography traces Mayer Amschel Rothschild (1744-1812) from Frankfurt's Judengasse — coin dealer, Court Agent to the immensely wealthy Elector of Hesse-Cassel in 1769 — to founder of 'M A Rothschild und Söhne' in 1810, the partnership that launched his five sons' banking network.
ai_summary:
AI review of the Rothschild Archive's biography of Mayer Amschel Rothschild (1744-1812), read in full:
- The family name traces to Izaak Elchanan Rothschild (1577), named for the house 'zum roten Schild' ('at the sign of the red shield') in Frankfurt's Judengasse, home and business center until the early 19th century.
- Born 1744 in the Judengasse, Mayer Amschel apprenticed under Jacob Wolf Oppenheimer in Hanover (1757), returned to Frankfurt (1763), dealt rare coins, and won the patronage of Crown Prince Wilhelm of Hesse — becoming 'Court Agent' in 1769 managing the Elector of Hesse-Cassel's finances.
- After the French Revolution he handled Britain's payments for Hessian mercenaries; when Napoleon invaded Hesse (1806) and Wilhelm IX went into exile, Rothschild continued as his banker, invested funds in London, and profited circumventing Napoleon's continental blockade.
- In 1810 he renamed the firm 'M A Rothschild und Söhne,' partnering with his four Frankfurt sons (Nathan Mayer Rothschild already established in Manchester and London); he died September 19, 1812, and was posthumously ennobled by Austria's Francis I in 1817.
- Record summary's early-history claims (1744-1812, Judengasse, 1810 firm, five sons' network) verified accurate; the later claims — sovereign-debt underwriting, financing Britain's Napoleonic war effort, today's Rothschild & Co, and 'owns no central banks' — are not established by this biography page.
